role.altitude: The clinical neuropsychologist keeps judging surgical risks, explaining them to teams and families, and giving therapy; collecting pre-surgical results, working prediction models by hand, writing patient letters and typing session notes shrink.
skills_to_grow: Explaining predicted risks with numbers patients understand
role.ambitious_version: A neuropsychologist whose patients go into surgery with the risks in plain words on paper, and whose notes are done when the session ends.

tasks.short: Gather pre-surgical results, compute predicted decline, identify the risks of neurological surgical procedures such as epilepsy surgery, communicate them to the surgical team, write, approve and send a plain-language risk letter, and discuss it with the patient and family.

steps.what: Neuropsychologist gathers pre-surgical test results, language lateralisation findings and the planned procedure
Neuropsychologist computes predicted memory and naming decline with published prediction models
Neuropsychologist identifies the risks of the neurological surgical procedure for this patient, weighing predictions, reserve and daily-life demands
Neuropsychologist communicates the risks to the surgical team at the multidisciplinary meeting
Neuropsychologist writes a plain-language letter on the risks for the patient

loop.input: The risk section of the signed neuropsychological report and the neuropsychologist's notes on this patient.
loop.output: A draft letter in plain language with the main risks, their size in words and numbers, and what they mean for daily life.
loop.check: Every risk and figure must match the signed report; the neuropsychologist rewrites anything that could mislead.
loop.stop: The neuropsychologist approves the letter, or writes it by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each patient's risks, life situation and reading level differ.

steps.what: Neuropsychologist checks and approves the final letter
Neuropsychologist sends the approved letter to the patient through the patient portal
Neuropsychologist discusses the risks with the patient and family and answers questions

approvals.approved_version: The letter text as approved by the neuropsychologist in s6, addressed to the patient in the record; any edit needs a new approval before sending.

tasks.design: The patient record gathers pre-surgical test scores, language lateralisation findings and the planned procedure on one screen. A validated calculation sheet applies the published prediction models to the scores, and the neuropsychologist checks the inputs. Weighing the risks for this patient and telling the surgical team stay with the neuropsychologist. A drafting step turns the risk section of the signed report into a plain-language letter, every figure matching the report. The neuropsychologist approves it and sends that version through the patient portal before the conversation with the patient and family, which stays personal. No software answers patients' questions about surgery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results sat in several places and patient letters were written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Record overviews, calculation sheets and drafting checked against the signed report.
tasks.still_hard: Patients for whom no prediction model fits.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a patient weigh seizure freedom against a memory risk.

ambition.what: Give every surgical candidate a written risk summary, not only those who ask.

tasks.altitude: Less gathering and letter writing; judging and talking stay.

reach.learn: Whether patients arrive at consent better prepared.

evidence.claim: Published models predict memory and naming decline after epilepsy surgery from pre-surgical scores.
The psychologist stays accountable for AI-drafted text.

assumptions: Boundary: identifying and communicating surgical risks; writing the full neuropsychological report (task 22224) and comparing progress before and after surgery (task 22207) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s5: the risk section of the signed report from task 22224.
Input contract for s2: the calculation sheet validated once against the published models by the department.
Judging, telling the team, approving, sending and the patient conversation keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of surgical candidates per year.
research_questions: Do patients recall the main risks better at consent?

incremental.description: Neuropsychologist checks the calculation sheet when a model is updated.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few candidates and complex cases; high: a regular surgical program with standard letters.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the session from the last note, provide psychotherapy, behavior therapy or counseling interventions, record and sign the session note, and select and send between-session exercises.

steps.what: Neuropsychologist prepares the session from the last note and homework
Neuropsychologist provides psychotherapy, behavior therapy or counseling interventions to the patient with a neurological disorder

loop.input: The neuropsychologist's spoken summary after the session.
loop.output: A draft session note in the record's template: themes, interventions, progress on goals and homework.
loop.check: The neuropsychologist corrects the draft line by line; goals named must exist in the treatment plan.
loop.stop: The neuropsychologist signs the note, or types it by hand when the draft is poor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Spoken summaries vary in order and wording.

steps.what: Neuropsychologist checks and signs the session note
Neuropsychologist selects between-session exercises for the patient
Neuropsychologist sends the selected exercises through the patient portal

approvals.approved_version: The exercise set chosen by the neuropsychologist in s5 for this patient; any change needs a new choice before sending.

tasks.design: The record opens on the last session note and the homework given, so preparing takes less searching. Therapy stays fully personal. After the session the neuropsychologist speaks a short summary, and a speech-to-note step drafts the note in the template; the neuropsychologist corrects and signs it. Only the summary is recorded, never the session, and the audio is deleted once the note is signed. Between-session exercises come from a department library and are sent through the patient portal instead of printed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed after each session and exercises were printed.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech-driven reporting in mental health care and patient portals with exercise libraries.
tasks.still_hard: Sessions where the main work is emotional, not structured.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a patient accept a changed self after brain injury.

reach.learn: Whether portal exercises are done more often.

evidence.claim: 24 of 25 large Dutch mental health providers use speech-driven reporting.
In a child mental health clinic median admin time per encounter fell from 27 to 10 minutes with ambient voice notes.

assumptions: Boundary: therapy and counseling for the patient; education and counseling for families (task 22221) and rehabilitation plans (task 22210) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s5: an exercise library kept by the department.
The clinic case recorded whole encounters; here only a spoken summary is drafted, so a smaller cut is assumed.
Therapy, signing and sending keep their full time.
unknowns: How many patients use the portal.
research_questions: Is note time per session lower without poorer notes?

incremental.description: Neuropsychologist adds exercises to the department library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short notes with many corrections; high: longer notes drafted well and regular exercises.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
